My first ever Korean BBQ, and honestly, what a way to be introduced to it. If you’ve never tried Korean BBQ before, the concept is simple ? a grill sits right in the centre of your table, and the food is cooked in front of you. At Daol, the staff take care of all of that for you, which made the whole experience completely relaxed and stress-free. They were attentive, friendly, and genuinely seemed to enjoy making sure we were having a great time. Nothing was too much trouble.
The banchan (side dishes) that arrived alongside our meal were a real highlight ? varied, flavourful, and the perfect accompaniment to the main event. But the star of the show? The sirloin steak. I don’t say this lightly: it was the best sirloin I have ever tasted. Perfectly cooked, unbelievably moist, and so tender it practically melted in your mouth. The quality of the meat speaks for itself.
Whether you’re a Korean BBQ veteran or a complete first-timer like I was, Daol is a must-visit. If you’re heading to Myeongdong, do yourself a favour and make this a priority stop ? you won’t regret it.

We always stay at the InterContinental Parnas whenever we visit Seoul, whether for business or leisure. During our recent 7-day stay, I decided ? for the first time ? to try the main breakfast restaurant, Grand Kitchen. I went about 15 minutes before closing, just planning to have a cup of coffee and a couple of boiled eggs, nothing elaborate. Upon arrival, the hostess politely checked my room number, informed the team that I was an Ambassador guest, and led me to a table. She offered coffee or tea and mentioned that the kitchen was serving poached eggs with avocado that morning. Since I love avocado, I simply requested a double portion of avocado without the eggs. She looked confused but said she would check with the kitchen.

While waiting, I walked around and admired the impressive breakfast selection. I picked up some eggs and made myself a glass of fresh green juice. However, when I returned to my table, I was shocked to see a plate of avocado that was clearly spoiled?brown, mushy slices that should never have been served to any guest, let alone one at a hotel of this standard. To make things worse, the coffee I had ordered earlier never arrived.

I approached the barista section to request a simple black coffee, but the young man informed me that breakfast service had ended and he could no longer make one. This was frustrating, considering I could have easily enjoyed attentive service and unlimited coffee at the club lounge on the 34th floor.

Overall, this experience was very disappointing. I understand that it was close to closing time, but that should never justify cold service or food that’s unfit to be served. Guests deserve care and hospitality regardless of the hour. Sadly, this visit left me feeling unwelcome ? and I decided not to return to the main breakfast restaurant again.

First, I have attached a brochure they have at the front of the restaurant that I sadly missed when we came in.  It gives a little background behind the naming of the courses and some Buddhist ideals.  

Second, if you want some of the fancier meals, you have to book in advance, but also let them know three days before that you want those meals.  The instructions in the menu are a little unclear, saying “parties more than four, but less than eight”, but if you want those pricier meals, you should book ahead.

Thirdly, I think it was interesting to try the foods in different ways.  I tried to try each dish individually, with different combos, and in different orders and it was definitely adding to the experience, given that each one yielded a different result.  Even if you find the experience a little unpalatable, try to finish every dish because it is very poor in Buddhist culture (and any Michelin star restaurant), to leave food behind.  

Finally, pricier doesn’t always mean better.  We were disappointed that we were unable to get the experience, however it turned out to be a bit of a blessing, because if you are not really familiar with temple food, even the less comprehensive meals can be a little challenging to finish.  

I think Korea sometimes is a little hard to navigate due to the lack of instruction, so I hope this review can help you enjoy the experience a bit more than we did!  :)

This was the restaurant I was most excited to try in Seoul. The first time we came, the restaurant was actually closed - be wary of the hours posted on Google. Google made it seem like the restaurant was open but Apple Maps showed that it was closed, so we decided to check anyway and Google turned out to be wrong. If you do wind up in the scenario, don’t worry because Insadong has several other great options for vegans. 

So, we wound up coming back a couple days later and barely got seated! We ended up coming into the restaurant about 45 minutes before the staff was going to close the restaurant for a midday break. We promised them that we eat really fast and it was our last day in Seoul, so the staff graciously sat us down. We were so grateful for their kindness and understanding!

In typical fashion, we ended up ordering a lot of food and the server was laughing as she was serving us - the meal service was really fast! They were even more shocked when we finished everything, haha! We ordered kimchi dumplings, tteokbokki, jjajangmyeon, fried chicken in a sweet & spicy sauce, and mushroom roll in hot sauce. We both loved everything! If I had to pick favorites, it would be between the jjajangmyeon and the fried chicken in sweet and spicy sauce. Though, the mushrooms were also great! Honestly, nothing was disappointing. 

The atmosphere is also rather interesting. They had an international vegan cooking channel playing on TV and lots of pamphlets and art about veganism, which made me happy and LOL. The restroom is also very clean. 

I would definitely come again if in Seoul and 100% recommend the food to vegans and non-vegans alike.

When we traveling to a new city, we love to get an overview of the city via a revolving restaurant.  There is no car access to Seoul Tower, which is where  N-Grill is located.  You have to either hike up the mountain, take public transportation, or take a Cable Car.

Both the restaurant and our travel guide suggested taking the cable car, but said we should get there 30 minutes in advance of our reservation.  But when we arrived at the Cable Car, the wait was over 75 minutes.  Add on the wait for the Seoul Tower elevator and we arrived at the restaurant more than an hour after our reservation.  We were initially thrilled that they honored our reservation.  But as soon as dinner began we noticed that the service was unusually fast, with courses arriving long before we finished the prior course.  Even the wine pairing could not keep up.  Our six course dinner (which was delicious)  was served in less than 40 minutes.  

The restaurant revolves once an hour, so we had yet to see the whole city.  We tried to order a glass of wine so that we could enjoy over the next 20 minutes.  But we were told that we exceeded our two hour time allocation for our reservation.  Huh!  What two hour time allocation?  We were asked to pay the bill and leave.  To top it off, every table we could see in either direction was empty.

What was supposed to be loverly dinner treat turned in an expensive night of aggravation.

This place was overpriced and not worthy of the cost.  If I could give it 0 stars I would.  We went there last night.  The only way to get to the top of the mountain is to walk uphill for 1 mile or take the tram which had a 1 1/2 hour wait.  They don't tell you this when you make the reservation and they charge you $50000 KRW per person to set up the reservation.  It is non refundable 24 hours out so if you can't get up there, to bad.  We were late for our reservation, but they still honored it since they knew there were issues getting up to the restaurant.  Once we arrived we were seated.  They had a prix fix menu that ran about $470,000 KRW per couple.  This included one glass of champagne.  The food was mediocre in taste at best.  The hot items were not hot - barely warm and we were rushed through dinner.  When I asked them to slow down they said they couldn't since we had several courses to get through.  It was not a pleasant dining experience, the staff was a bit aloof and the food lacked taste compared to some of the other restaurants we experienced in Seoul.  For $370 US I would think they would be more attentive to our needs.  They didn't even keep our water glass full.  Unfortunately, this was our last night In Seoul and not a great way to end this part of our trip.  The trip down was the same mess.  Wait in line forever to get back down on the tram.  Don't waste your time with this restaurant.  It's not worth the hassle.  It is just a tourist trap.

One of the best neapolitan pizzas in Korea. Maybe even top 10 in Asia. 
The pizza chef have for many years received awards for making authentic neapolitan pizzas and they are just as good and sometimes better than the ones you get around Napoli. If anyone tells you otherwise they simply dont know what a good neapolitan pizza is supposed to be like. Unfortunately many people think any thin crust pizza is neapolitan and expect american style pizza.  
The pizza here does everything right and deserves all the praise they get. The crust is both crunchy and chewy while being perfectly thin. The sauce is excellent and is made of real tomatoes. Not just the generic puree based sauce you find on more well knowns pizza chains. Toppings are also of high quality and the amount is jsut like a neapolitan pizza is supposed to have.

They also sell some pasta dishes and some salads.

Note that they do not take reservations and you must sign up for a waiting queue should the place be full. You will get a sms or email when your number is up. They may deny you if they know they cant take more customers before closing time. And that is where the confusion from some other reviews may come from. The restaurant see how long the waiting line is, you dont. People who are waiting isnt standing at the restaurant since they will get notified on sms or email. Also the language barrier is real so dont just assume they are trying to be rude when denying you with limited English skills.
From my experience they are very friendly and very helpful. Always felt welcomed here.

The restaurant’s atmosphere definitely screamed fine dining or a lovely place to bring your date for a romantic/special occasion. 

I ordered the fresh mozzarella and beefsteak tomatoes (?18,000), prime filet mignon, and mac n’ cheese (?19,000). 

The caprese salad was impressive. The mozzarella and tomatoes were both huge, that like the ones you expect from a boujee steakhouse. The mozzarella tasted very fresh “expensive”. The tomato was the not mushy type, which I personally prefer. Therefore, the softness of the mozzarella and the hardness of the tomatoes really complemented each other. The dish was seasoned with an original salt and pepper with a simple pesto sauce on top of the dish. 

For the entre, we ordered the US prime filet mignon. There is a distinguishable difference between the “Korean steak” and “US prime steak”. I personally like the US one a lot better because it was so big in size and juicy. I went with a medium temp on my steak and the exterior was crispy, just the way I like it. You immediately notice that the steak cuts like butter and melts in your mouth. The steak was also seasoned and cooked perfectly. For a side dish, we certainly recommend the creamy spinach dish/lobster mac and cheese. 
We decided to order both and it was not a mistake. Just like the name suggests, the creamy spinach was really rich and thick in flavor. The mac and cheese, however, was my favorite between those two. The mac had a crispy golden top and the actual sauce was so creamy and cheesy. The lobster was also cooked well and was cut out in adequate sizes, so it really amplified the dish. 

All in all, though this restaurant is more of a costly place, it is definitely a go-to date spot.

Stepping into Hue 135 in Itaewon, Korea, is like entering a realm of elegance and sophistication. The restaurant’s modern decor is a perfect blend of chic minimalism and luxurious comfort. Soft, ambient lighting casts a warm glow over the tastefully arranged tables, creating an intimate atmosphere ideal for a romantic dinner or a special celebration. The stylish interior, with its subtle nods to both Western and Korean aesthetics, sets the stage for an exceptional dining experience.

Course menu included a sashimi of the day, tartare, chawanmushi, and a trio of meats: charcoal-grilled hanwoo special cuts, nook rubbed hanwoo tenderloin steak, dry aged hanwoo steak (30 days) which were cuts of meats that one wouldn’t be able to get an any ordinary steakhouse.  These fine cuts were followed by a savory truffle mushroom steamed rice set and a 48hr based short-rib.  The dessert was a play on a korean candy called yuht and Hue135’s own beef jerky - which was crispy and light.  

Hue 135 is more than just a steak restaurant; it is a fine dining experience that caters to all the senses. The combination of exquisite food, exceptional service, and a luxurious yet inviting atmosphere makes it a standout destination in Itaewon. Whether you are celebrating a special occasion or simply indulging in a night of culinary delight.  The steaks are outstanding and every dish that compliments the meat.

I was actually looking forward to some Malaysian food tonight, especially if one wants something other than the usual Korean bbq or soup. 

Two of us ordered two drinks (a pop and a mango drink), a roti (Malaysian bread), a Nasi Lemak Rendang chicken and a Nasi Goreng Black Pepper beef.

Nasi Lemak is known as the national dish in Malaysia. The classic version is coconut rice served with chicken in sambal sauce. Since this one was labelled "rendang", the chicken should be in a Rendang sauce. The plate should come also with roasted peanuts and fried crispy anchovies, slices cucumbers and a tamarind sauce on the side.

The plate we got did not have any hint of coconut in the rice. The red tamarind sauce was okay but lacking in tamarind flavor.

Nasi Goreng (fried rice) typically comes with crackers (krupuk), cucumbers, deep-fried shallots (Bawang Goreng) etc. The rice should be fried with egg, and flavored with a mixture of spices (bumbu) - the exact spices used would depend on the cook's preference, but the rice should be flavored with the sweet soy sauce (kecap manis).

The plate that we got had a lot of very tender black peppered beef, which was nice. But the rice was not nasi goreng (fried rice). It resembled a cooked rice mixed with some rice (tumeric?) and was not flavorful. There were no shallots. However the crackers were light and crispy.

Roti Canai or Roti Prata is the flaky on the outside, light and soft on the inside, multi-layered Malaysian bread with origin from India. The one we got was flaky but doughy inside - not enough layers!

We got the attention of our waitress and ordered dinner.  My wife got the French onion soup and I ordered a Caesar Salad.  We split the escargot.  All of it was fantastic!  The escargots were served in the shells and had a great herbed flavor without the bath of garlic butter that makes them so heavy sometimes.  My wife's lamb chops and my steak came out next. We boxed up half of the meal and had a very delicious Tiramisu for dessert.  I ate the rest for lunch at work later.  The food was exceptional!  So, why not five stars? I'm certainly not arrogant enough to demand it be, and we love living in Korea.  This brings me to my second minor ding.  If you run a restaurant that charges $200 a person, please have an available translator.  That corkage fee would have saved my $75 and got me a better wine because, lets face it.  This restaurant is exorbitantly priced, by any standard!  Peter Lugars?  Nope.  Craft Steak?  Nope. I have just eaten at this restaurant. It was not my first choice but having endured a 7 hour journey from Jinju that should have taken 4 I was in no mood to trek halfway across Gangnam-gu to find my first choice.

The restaurant is situated opposite the Intercontinental COEX where I was staying. Initially I wasn’t sure it was the correct place but the crowds outside and the pig snout seemed to give it away.

I was greeted by a guy that I can only describe as looking a bit like Yoda. I mean that in a good way....the kind of guy that guides you through your journey only with more enthusiasm.

He explained in broken English that I needed two people but I assured him that although I was one. I would eat for two (having not eaten for over 24 hours).

I was going to order more than I did but he told me it was too much for one and so I settled on the pork belly and the glazed pork rib.

I was comfortable using the chopsticks and cooking myself having visited Korea several times a year for the past 14 years but he insisted on cooking much to the disdain and disapproval of the ladies clearing tables.

At one point he disappeared and one of the ladies came over and turned some of the cuts of meat then told me she was very busy so I should do it myself. There are times when this would annoy me but I just found it funny as I hadn’t asked her to do anything in the first place and was quite in control.

The pork belly was good but I have better but the glazed rib was divine. I came close to ordering another but the lady came and whisked away the coals before I could. It would have been pure greed though.

Side dishes were lovely and I especially enjoyed the kimchi as it really cut through some of the fattyness of the pork and had a good kick to it.

I think had I been served by another person my rating would probably be lower but the gentleman that took care of me was such a nice friendly guy it’s got to be a 5star review.

The final bill with two bottles of beer was KRW 50,000 which I thought was good for a city dinner, I pay far more for a similar meal in London or even some of the minor U.K. towns and villages.

Next time I’m in Seoul I’m scheduling a dinner here.
